sumInsured: Not specified in provided extract (Sum Insured is as per Policy Schedule; examples show ₹5,00,000 in illustrations)

great.name: Room Rent
great.quote: The eligible Room Rent or Room Category applicable for the Insured Person under the Policy is No limit, which means that there is no separate restriction on Room Charges incurred towards stay during Hospitalization
great.explanation: Room rent is on a No limit basis with no separate restriction on room category/charges during hospitalization. This reduces the risk of out-of-pocket costs and avoids room-rent linked deductions.

great.name: ICU Charges
great.quote: Intensive Care Unit Charges (ICU Charges): The eligible ICU Charges applicable for the Insured Person under the Policy is No limit, which means that there is no separate restriction on ICU Charges incurred towards stay in ICU during Hospitalization.
great.explanation: ICU charges are covered with No limit and no separate cap for ICU stay during hospitalization. This is important because ICU bills can be very high and caps often create large shortfalls.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: automatically make the re-instatement of up to the base Sum Insured unlimited times in a policy year... Recharge amount can be utilized for same illness as well as different Illnesses.
great.explanation: Base Sum Insured can be reinstated unlimited times in a policy year. The recharged amount can be used for the same illness as well as different illnesses, which is stronger than most restore benefits.

great.name: No Claim Bonus
great.quote: enhance the Sum Insured by 50% flat... In the event of a Claim there is no impact on the accrual of Cumulative Bonus.
great.explanation: Sum Insured is enhanced by a flat 50% as cumulative bonus. Even if a claim happens, there is no impact on the accrual of the cumulative bonus, so the bonus does not get reduced/reset.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: The Plus Benefit will be applicable only after exhaustion of Base Sum Insured.
great.explanation: Plus Benefit becomes applicable only after the Base Sum Insured is exhausted. This effectively provides an additional insurer-funded buffer once your base cover is fully used.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy inception with the insurer. This is within common market ranges, but it delays coverage for known conditions.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illness treatment is not covered for the first 30 days from the first policy commencement date, except for accidents. This is a standard waiting period and mainly affects early claims soon after buying the policy.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting Period
good.quote: shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Specified illnesses are excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage. This is a common condition and means some listed treatments wont be payable in the first 2 years.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: For a period of 60 days immediately prior to the Insured Persons date of admission to the Hospital
good.explanation: Medical expenses are covered for 60 days immediately prior to the date of admission. This helps reimburse diagnostic tests and consultations leading up to hospitalization.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: For a period of 90 days immediately after the Insured Persons date of discharge from the hospital
good.explanation: Medical expenses are covered for 90 days immediately after the date of discharge. This supports follow-up treatment and medicines after hospitalization.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure 	I to Policy Terms & Conditions).
bad.explanation: Items listed as Non-Medical Items in Annexure I are excluded from payment. This can increase out-of-pocket costs for common consumables unless another benefit/add-on specifically covers them.

bad.name: Domiciliary Exclusions
bad.quote: Any Medical Expenses incurred for the treatment in relation to any of the following diseases shall not be payable under this Benefit : ... Diabetes Mellitus... Hypertension... Asthma... All Psychiatric or Psychosomatic Disorders... Arthritis, Gout and Rheumatism.
bad.explanation: Domiciliary hospitalization does not pay for home-treatment expenses for several common conditions like Diabetes Mellitus, Hypertension, Asthma, psychiatric disorders, and Arthritis/Gout/Rheumatism. This significantly limits the usefulness of domiciliary cover for chronic illnesses.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: The Co-payment proportion (If opted) shall be borne by the Insured Person on each Claim
bad.reference: General Conditions under Benefits Covered, point 5 and Clause 3.2.29
bad.explanation: A co-payment applies if opted, meaning you bear a proportion of each claim. Any co-pay increases your out-of-pocket share on every claim and is a negative feature even when optional.
